programs.title: Genomics, AI and the Future of Work at the Genome Campus
outcomes: Explain how agent-managed DAOs route tasks while humans keep voting rights
Map five ways genomic data work could affect union members' jobs
Draft a worker question set for an AI governance consultation

sessions.activity: Read the DAO charter; identify the six human-reserved powers and discuss why they are never delegated to agents.
Review an evidence summary on AI in genomics workplaces; practice separating claims from cited sources.
Role-play a debate: agents draft a training proposal, members amend and vote on enacting it.
Trace how the Task Router assigns work; draft member-friendly language for a workload policy.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised pre/post confidence scores and short text answers about workplace AI concerns, aggregated with no names or employers attached.
programs.consent: Participation is voluntary; learners sign a plain-language consent form covering anonymised contribution of survey and exercise answers, with opt-out at any session.

programs.title: Code of Life: Exploring Genomics on the Genome Campus
outcomes: Describe what a genome is and why Hinxton matters in science history
Explain that AI tools help scientists but people make decisions
Design a simple rule for fair sharing of scientific benefits

sessions.activity: Decode a simple DNA sequence with paper strips; discuss how computers at this campus helped read the human genome.
Compare the DAO's rules to classroom rules; identify which decisions stay with people and which helpers can do.
In teams, write a short proposal for a genomics project that helps the local community; vote as a class.
Create a poster tracking the class's project outcomes and mark progress on a big chart.

programs.data_shared: Anonymous class tallies of votes and quiz answers only; no individual names, photos or writing samples collected.
programs.consent: Guardian/parent consent forms required for all data activities; teachers explain privacy in plain language, and parents may opt out while students still take part in all activities.

programs.title: Human Governance of AI: Field Methods from a DAO Cell
outcomes: Apply the agent-operates / human-decides split to programme design
Use evidence summaries to brief decision-makers honestly
Facilitate a proposal cycle with community stakeholders

sessions.activity: Workshop: turn a monitored evidence stream into a one-page brief distinguishing sourced facts from inference.
Run a mock proposal cycle: agent-drafted proposals, structured stakeholder debate, human-only final vote.
Design a task-routing workflow for a multi-partner campaign using working groups.
Define measurable outcomes and a tracking dashboard for a real NGO programme.

programs.data_shared: Aggregated evaluation scores and anonymised workflow templates contributed to a shared methods library, stripped of organisational identifiers.
programs.consent: Staff consent via organisational agreement plus individual opt-in for the shared methods library; no beneficiary or partner data enters shared models.

programs.title: Data Stewardship and Public-Good AI for Nonprofits
outcomes: State the principles of governing AI as a public good
Assess which decisions a nonprofit board must reserve to humans
Plan a transparent progress-reporting cycle for donors

sessions.activity: Board exercise: map your nonprofit's decisions against the six human-reserved powers; flag any risks.
Case study: how agent-drafted grants work when humans hold enactment and treasury powers.
Sketch a working-group structure and task routing plan for a small nonprofit team.
Build a simple outcome dashboard template to report measurable impact to funders.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised board self-assessment scores and dashboard templates added to a shared open library, with no beneficiary or financial details included.
programs.consent: Participation under a signed organisational MOU; individual contributions anonymised before sharing, with any board able to withdraw its materials at any time.
